QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_21

question.text: A trader buys a bull call spread: long call at Rs. 99 for Rs. 4 and short call at Rs. 104 for Rs. 1.50. If the underlying expires at Rs. 101, what is the P&L?

explanation.text: The Logic: A bull call spread is long a lower-strike call and short a higher-strike call, with limited profit and limited loss (workbook pp. 167-168). At expiry Rs. 101: long 99 call payoff = 101 - 99 = 2; short 104 call expires worthless. Net premium paid = 4 - 1.50 = 2.50. P&L = 2 - 2.50 = -Rs. 0.50 (loss). The Trap: Rs. 2.00 ignores the net premium. Loss of Rs. 2.50 ignores the long-call payoff. Profit of Rs. 0.50 reverses the sign. Note: Between the two strikes, only the long call has intrinsic value while the net premium remains a cost.
